newsitem.title: USA: Photos of slain child hard to find in Colorado.
newsitem.headline: Photos of slain child hard to find in Colorado.

text.p: Many Colorado stores refused Monday to sell a supermarket tabloid that is running coroner's photos of slain 6-year-old JonBenet Ramsey because their customers let them know the subject was too sensitive.

Monday's edition of The Globe was not available at 240 "7-11" convenience stores, where management decided not to sell the issue. "Our customers in Colorado let us know. They were polite, very nice, but the feelings ran very high," said Karen Roskopf, spokeswoman for Dallas-based Southland Corp.'s "7-11" stores, explaining why the tabloid was not on sale.
The chain's management sent an advisory to stores in the rest of the country to allow them to decide on an individual basis if they wanted to sell the tabloid, she said.

Leading supermarket chains in Colorado also declined to sell the Globe in the region but a manager at one Newsland store in Denver described sales as "gangbusters" because of the issue's availability.

Globe editor Tony Frost, has defended the use of the photos, saying they were crime scene photos rather than autopsy photos of the juvenile beauty queen and publication was necessary because so little information was coming from police in Boulder. But the family condemned the Globe for running the photos, calling it a "ghoulish" act.
The Boulder County sheriff's office launched an invetigation over the weekend of how the photos were leaked to the Globe.

Roy McCutchen, the president of Photo Craft Laboratories, which processes film for the coroner's office, said in a statement he "was appalled that anyone would stoop so low as to provide images of this nature to anyone outside of the official pipeline." He said his company was "aggressively particpating" in the probe into how the photos were leaked.
The investigation into the murder continued Monday, Boulder city spokeswoman Leslie Aaholm said. No arrests have been made and no suspects have been named.

Newsweek magazine said police have identified suspects, narrowing the field to seven or eight in the strangling of JonBenet, who was found dead in her Boulder home the day after Christmas. Her body was found by her father in the basement of the family's 15-room home some eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.
Published reports said there appeared to be no forced entry into the home and local authorities played down remarks by the mother, Patricia Ramsey, that there was a "killer on the loose" in Boulder.
